chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Cleanliness of the clothes removes anxiety and grief, and it is a purifier for the prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and psychological benefit of wearing clean clothes in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, links physical cleanliness to spiritual tranquility, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *taharah* (purity) as both a ritual prerequisite and a psychological remedy. By describing clean garments as a 'purifier for prayer,' it underscores the holistic nature of worship in Shia jurisprudence, where external neatness complements internal devotion. This concept is often cited by scholars to justify the recommendation (*mustahabb*) of wearing one's best clothes for congregational prayers and daily acts of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The clean clothes remove the stress and the grief, and it is a cleanliness for the Salat (Prayer)’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Clean clothes remove sadness and it is of cleanliness for Salat (prayer).”’
